question: The first Indian to win the All England Badminton Championship in 1980 ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakash Padukone**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prakash Padukone became the **first Indian to win the prestigious All England Badminton Championship in 1980.**
 
• Prakash Padukone defeated Indonesia's Liem Swie King, a top player of that era, in the** final with a score of 15–3, 15–10.**
 
• Along with the All England title, Padukone won many other international titles and became a trailblazer for Indian badminton players worldwide.
 
• He was honored with the **Arjuna Award in 1972**, recognizing his excellence and contribution to Indian sports, particularly badminton.
 
• **In 1982, Prakash Padukone received the Padma Shri,** India's fourth-highest civilian award, for his outstanding achievements in badminton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kiran Bedi**

 
 
• Kiran Bedi became the **first woman to join the Indian Police Service (IPS) in 1972**, breaking gender barriers in law enforcement.
 
• She was awarded the **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Government Service in 1994** for her pioneering reforms in the Indian prison system, particularly at Tihar Jail.
 
• She was Inspector General of Tihar Jail, she introduced several innovative reforms focused on education, meditation, and rehabilitation for inmates.
 
• Kiran Bedi served as the **Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry** from 2016 to 2021, contributing to the administration and governance of the Union Territory.
 
 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar**
 
 
• Sachin Tendulkar is the only cricketer in the world to **score 100 international centuries (51 in Test cricket and 49 in One-Day Internationals).**
 
• He was at the age of 17, Tendulkar became the youngest Indian to score a Test century, achieving this milestone against England at Old Trafford in 1990.
 
• In 2010, Tendulkar became the **first player in history to score a double century in a One-Day International**, against South Africa.
 
• He was **awarded the Bharat Ratna,** India's highest civilian honor, in 2014, becoming the first sportsperson to receive this recognition.
 
 
 
• **Dhyan Chand**
 
 
• Dhyan Chand earned the nickname **"The Wizard"** for his extraordinary ball control and dribbling abilities on the hockey field.
 
• He won **three Olympic gold medals** in field hockey for India in** 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles), and 1936 (Berlin).**
 
• Dhyan Chand is regarded as one of the greatest field hockey players in history, known for his exceptional goal-scoring skills.
 
• His birthday, **August 29, is celebrated as National Sports Day** in India, honoring his contributions to Indian sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other famous Indian badminton players:**

 
 
• **Pullela Gopichand**

 
 
• He won the All England Badminton Championship in 2001, becoming the second Indian to achieve this feat after Prakash Padukone.
 
 
 
• **Saina Nehwal**
 
 
• Saina Nehwal became the **first Indian badminton player to win an Olympic medal **(bronze) at the 2012 London Olympics and has held the world No. 1 ranking in women's singles.
 
 
 
• **P.V. Sindhu**:
 
 
• P.V. Sindhu won a **silver medal **at the 2016 Rio Olympics, a** bronze **at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, and became the first Indian to win the BWF World Championships (gold in 2019).
 
 
 
• **Kidambi Srikanth**
 
 
• Kidambi Srikanth became the **first Indian male badminton player to win four Super Series **titles in a calendar year (2017), and he achieved the world No. 1 ranking in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Lakshya Sen**
 
 
• A rising star in Indian badminton, **Lakshya Sen won the bronze medal at the 2021 BWF World Championships** and the gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.
